market_snapshot.breadth_notes: All futures figures are Friday premarket (~5am ET). All other internals describe Thursday's prior regular session: S&P 500 +0.19% at 7,666.45, snapping a 3-day losing streak; ~56% of issues advancing vs 41.5% declining (ratio derived from those sourced figures); tech +0.8% led on semis, biotech lagged; 53-65% of stocks above their 20/50/100/200-day SMAs. market_snapshot.notes: Fri 4:00am PT premarket: futures higher ahead of the 8:30am ET jobs report (Dow +0.51%, S&P +0.5%, Nasdaq-100 +0.83%); 10Y at 5.236% off Thursday's 24-year high ~5.34% after the Jefferson dovish pivot; Brent $101.14 premarket (-1.1%) after Thursday's +4% run to $102.31 on US Mideast buildup; gold ~$4,157; BTC ~$86,300; DXY at 18-month high.

headlines.headline: Nike reported fiscal Q1 after Thursday's close: revenue $11.21B (-4% y/y) missed ~$11.3B consensus while EPS $0.48 beat; Greater China -26% currency-neutral; full-year FY27 guide cut to revenue down high-single-digits and adjusted EPS $1.15-$1.35 vs $1.67 consensus, with a $2.5B savings plan. Shares down ~9% premarket, worst year on record.
headlines.why_it_matters: Revenue miss plus a much weaker full-year guide says the turnaround is taking longer than expected — a sentiment overhang for consumer discretionary at the open.

headlines.headline: Google launched Gemini 4 Argon, its most advanced AI model, priced at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens — undercutting rival frontier models; shares up ~1.3% premarket to $348.41 after a 16% slide since May. Separately, Google put TPU technology in orbit for the first time on a SpaceX rideshare.
headlines.why_it_matters: A credible frontier-model launch plus an orbital TPU demo gives the AI narrative fresh legs — supportive bid for megacap tech.

headlines.headline: New Mexico is reportedly seeking up to $40B in data-privacy penalties from Meta tied to the Cambridge Analytica matter; shares up marginally premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The $40B figure is a single reported ask, not a confirmed fine — treat as fragile; it adds legal-overhang noise on top of Thursday's relative weakness.

headlines.headline: Amazon is reportedly exploring shifting ~$8B of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips into a special-purpose vehicle and leasing them back.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source and unconfirmed — treat as fragile; if real, it would be a capex-light way to keep funding AI infrastructure, easing balance-sheet strain concerns.

headlines.headline: Nvidia up ~0.9% premarket (closed Thursday +1.09% at $230.86), carried by Micron's record quarter — revenue $54.2B and FY Q1 guide of ~$61.5B vs $56.8B consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: Micron's numbers are the strongest evidence yet AI memory capex is still accelerating — a direct sentiment tailwind for the AI-chip complex.

headlines.headline: Tesla reports Q3 2026 deliveries today (not yet released as of 4am PT). Company-compiled consensus: ~462k vehicles (median 463,406), about -7% y/y vs the record 497,099 in Q3 2025 when US EV credits were expiring; energy storage consensus 15.9 GWh (+27% y/y).
headlines.why_it_matters: Tesla's biggest near-term catalyst lands during today's session — the actual print will move the stock off expectations either way.

headlines.headline: ON Semiconductor agreed to buy Synaptics for $5.7B — revised down from $7B previously. ON +6.1%, SYNA +14% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: A lower agreed price reads as a buyer-friendly renegotiation — a modest positive for ON while still a takeover premium for SYNA.

headlines.headline: Moderna will replace Warner Bros. Discovery in the Nasdaq-100 effective Oct 9, as WBD completes its Paramount Skydance merger next week; MRNA +~2% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Index inclusion means mechanical buying from Nasdaq-100 trackers — a flow tailwind into the Oct 9 effective date.

headlines.headline: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson signaled patience Thursday — officials 'may need more time' before judging whether further hikes are needed — and October rate-hike odds fell to ~23-26% from ~70% Monday; Goldman pushed its next-hike call to December.
headlines.why_it_matters: The dovish pivot from the Fed's #2 drove Thursday's bond rebound off the 24-year yield high — and makes Friday's jobs report the swing factor for the Oct 27-28 meeting.

headlines.headline: Initial jobless claims held at 197,000 (unchanged, vs 200k expected) — a 10-week low — with continuing claims at a 3.5-year low ahead of today's September payrolls (consensus ~84-95k, unemployment 4.1%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Steady claims support the 'labor market stable' read — a neutral-to-positive backdrop heading into NFP, with little pre-emption of the report.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. Today, Friday Oct 2, is the last NYSE trading day; units begin trading on the Texas Stock Exchange on Oct 5 with the ticker unchanged. Carried: consensus Hold with $29.50 average target across six firms; Wall Street Zen downgrade to hold (Sep 26); $600M 6.75% senior notes due 2035 priced Sep 9. Thursday's $102 Brent is a mild sector tailwind.

watch_next: 8:30am ET: September jobs report (NFP consensus ~84-95k, unemployment 4.1%) — the week's main event; October hike odds at ~25% make it the swing factor.
Tesla Q3 deliveries drop today (~462k consensus, -7% y/y) — moves TSLA during the session.
Nike opens down ~9% after the Q1 miss and FY27 guide cut — watch consumer discretionary fallout.
USAC: last NYSE trading day today; units list on the Texas Stock Exchange Oct 5 (ticker unchanged).
10Y yield direction after Thursday's 24-year high (~5.34%) — the bond bid is still the index's boss.
analysis: The frame flipped on one speech: Jefferson's dovish pivot Thursday took October hike odds from ~70% to ~25% and knocked the 10Y off its 24-year high to ~5.24%, which is why futures are green into the open. That makes today's 8:30am ET jobs report the single swing factor — a hot print re-arms hike bets (Deutsche Bank flags exactly that), a soft one cements the pause. Stock-specific: the AI-capex paper trail stays signed (Micron's record quarter, ON/Synaptics) while the consumer turnaround story stalled (Nike's miss + guide cut, worst year on record). Meta has a double overhang: the OpenAI-threat weakness from earlier this week plus a single-source $40B penalties ask from New Mexico — the latter is fragile, treat accordingly. Signal vs noise: NFP, Tesla deliveries, and the Nike open are the signal; the META $40B ask, AMZN's $8B SPV report, and the Oracle/Tencent $7B chip lease (unconfirmed by both companies) are single-source noise until confirmed. Community read: the 1,655-point HN thread on Gemini 4 Argon confirms devs see Google back among the top three AI labs — constructive for the AI bid, not hype. Vs yesterday's briefs: the market went from 'good data is bad for bonds' (ISM prices-paid) to a Fed patience pivot — same 10Y level, opposite mood; Thursday's session snapped a 3-day losing streak with 56% breadth.

community_signals.takeaway: 1,655 points / 1,145 comments — the dev community sees Google back among the top three AI labs on intelligence, reinforcing constructive AI-infra sentiment rather than chasing benchmarks.
